routes.label: Equate the melted volume and cone capacity

question: An ice cream cone consists of a sphere of vanilla ice cream and a right circular cone that has the same diameter as the sphere. If the ice cream melts, it will exactly fill the cone. Assume that the melted ice cream occupies \(75\%\) of the volume of the frozen ice cream. What is the ratio of the cone’s height to its radius? (Note: A cone with radius \(r\) and height \(h\) has volume \(\frac{\pi r^2 h}{3},\) and a sphere with radius \(r\) has volume \(\frac{4\pi r^3}{3}.\))
solution:
Equal diameters mean that the sphere and the cone's circular base have the same radius. Call this radius \(r>0\), and let the cone's height be \(h>0\).

The melted ice cream has \(75\%=\frac34\) of the sphere's volume. Since it exactly fills the cone, the supplied volume formulas give
\[
\frac{\pi r^2h}{3}
=\frac34\left(\frac{4\pi r^3}{3}\right)
=\pi r^3.
\]
Because \(r>0\), we may divide by \(\pi r^2/3\), obtaining \(h=3r\). Therefore the height-to-radius ratio is \(\boxed{3:1}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
